items.followUp: Define Percentage-Mass/Volume and write its formula.

rubric.why: The definition compares the volume of solute with the volume of the solution.
rubric.description: Identify the two volumes used in Percentage-Volume/Volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying both the volume of solute and the volume of solution.

rubric.why: The volume ratio is multiplied by 100 to express it as a percentage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula, including multiplication by 100.

modelAnswer: Percentage-Volume/Volume is the volume of solute dissolved in 100 volumes of solution.
Percentage (v/v) = (volume of solute ÷ volume of solution) × 100.

items.followUp: Why is the atomic radius of potassium greater than that of sodium?

rubric.why: Sodium has a smaller atomic size and fewer occupied shells than potassium.
rubric.description: Compare the size or occupied shells of Na and K.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Na has a smaller atomic radius or fewer occupied electron shells.

rubric.why: Sodium’s outer electron is held more strongly, so more energy is needed to remove it.
rubric.description: Explain why Na has the higher ionization energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stronger nuclear attraction on Na’s outer electron to the greater energy needed to remove it.

modelAnswer: Na has a smaller atomic radius and fewer occupied electron shells than K.
Therefore, Na’s outer electron is closer to the nucleus and experiences stronger attraction, so more energy is needed to remove it.

rubric.description: Write the balanced equation for H₂ reacting with F₂.

items.followUp: Write any five characteristics of an electron beam (cathode rays).

rubric.why: Cathode rays propagate in straight lines.
rubric.description: State that cathode rays travel in straight lines.

rubric.why: Cathode rays consist of negatively charged particles.
rubric.description: State that cathode rays carry a negative charge.

rubric.why: Their negative charge makes them deflect towards the positive plate.
rubric.description: Describe their deflection in an electric field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are deflected towards the positive plate.

rubric.why: Cathode rays cause certain materials to fluoresce when they strike them.
rubric.description: State that cathode rays produce fluorescence.

rubric.why: An object in their path can block the rays and cast a shadow.
rubric.description: State that cathode rays cast shadows.

modelAnswer: Cathode rays travel in straight lines.
They are deflected by an electric field towards the positive plate.
They produce fluorescence when they strike certain materials.
They cast shadows when an object is placed in their path.

items.followUp: Define an element, a compound, a cation and an anion.

rubric.why: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that participates in chemical change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of an atom.

rubric.why: An ion has an electrical charge resulting from electron loss or gain.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an ion is charged due to loss or gain of electrons.

rubric.why: An unpaired electron is the defining feature of a free radical.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the presence of one or more unpaired electrons.

rubric.why: A molecule is an independently existing particle that retains the chemical properties of its substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable definition of a molecule.

modelAnswer: Atom: The smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction.
Ion: An atom or group of atoms carrying an electrical charge due to the loss or gain of electrons.
Free radical: An atom or group of atoms containing one or more unpaired electrons.
Molecule: The smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retains the chemical properties of that substance.
